applicability.reason: Supported. The row asserts that an arbitrary-precision Integer survives `((2 ** 200) + 1) - (2 ** 200)` as Integer(1) with NO representation Type split, and that backends agree. The recorded blocker was that only one backend existed, and a backend agreeing with ITSELF observes nothing. A second backend now exists: `iris-vm` compiles the expression to instructions and runs it on a stack machine, so the two reach the result by different execution paths. Comparison is over a semantic Observation rather than over runtime values, because IRIS-V1-CONFORMANCE-C068 forbids comparing heap addresses, object pointer values and private bytecode layout; identity-bearing values therefore render as their KIND, and floats render as BITS so a one-ulp divergence cannot hide. The harness reports fewer than two RUNNING backends as insufficient rather than as agreement, so a row cannot pass merely because a backend declined it.

expect.equivalence: Integer(1) with no representation Type split.
